digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III; Pakia (2005) App. VI

teaser.en: Its name is the sound you make spitting out the seed after sucking its little yellow fruit.

summary.en: *Mpwakapwaka* is a shrub of coastal forest and thicket with large leaves crowded at the tip and small round yellow fruits. Its fruit is sucked and spat out, and its names are among the most playful in Digo.

about.en: *Mpwakapwaka* is a shrub or small tree, often with a single stem crowned by a tuft of large, feathery compound leaves crowded at the tip, which gives it a slightly palm-like look. It bears small, round yellow fruits.

where.en: It grows in coastal forest and thicket.

uses.en: The fruits are edible: they are sucked for their pulp and the rest spat out.

culture.en: Both its names tell a story. *Mpwakapwaka* imitates the spitting sound made after sucking the fruit. Its other name, *mtsungurira kuzimu*, 'peeping into the underworld', refers to its very deep roots.

names.en: Pakia records two Digo names, *mpwakapwaka* and *mtsungurira kuzimu*. No Swahili or English common name has been recorded; botanists call it *Deinbollia borbonica*. The Mgombato dictionary gives *mpwakapwaka* to a different tree in the same family, the triangle-tops (*Blighia unijugata*), with the Swahili *mkukilemba* and *mwakamwatu*.

reason.en: Triangle-tops, which also carries the name mpwakapwaka

sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: an ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD thesis, Univ. Bayreuth, Appendix III (Digo–botanical name list) & Appendix VI (name semantics). https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf

digo_proposals.name: mpwakapwaka
digo_proposals.note: Mgombato and ICRAF give mpwakapwaka for Blighia unijugata
